analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי introduces the scene. הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ לָבוֹא sets the time, “as the sun was about to set,” and וְתַרְדֵּמָה נָפְלָה עַל אַבְרָם tells what happened, “a deep sleep fell on Abram.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ is followed by יְהִי, the short third-person masculine singular Qal form of הָיָה used in the wayyiqtol.

analysis.evidence: הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ לָבוֹא means “the sun was about to set,” fixing the time when a deep sleep fell on Abram.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial שׁ of the noun. The noun is common gender, singular, and in the absolute state.
